purpose: External-validity experiment: determine whether Rapture's accepted-engineering-throughput measurement remains meaningful on realistic engineering tasks drawn from an upstream third-party codebase, rather than only on Rapture-authored synthetic fixtures. Measures whether raising OpenCode concurrency from 1 worker to 2 produces measurable accepted-throughput scaling on the upstream-derived semver-core benchmark repository.
northStarQuestion: On a real upstream TypeScript/Node.js codebase with realistic engineering tasks, does increasing OpenCode concurrency from 1 worker to 2 workers produce measurable accepted engineering throughput scaling?

baseline.note: origin/main matched the expected research baseline SHA exactly. The literal token RAPTURE_RESEARCH_BASELINE_READY does not appear anywhere in the tree or history; the SHA is treated as authoritative.

modelSelection.constraint: OpenCode only. Codex must not be executed and must not consume quota. No paid provider experiment was authorized, so selection was restricted to free-tier OpenCode models.
modelSelection.reason: All three candidates answered a standalone probe with cost 0 and structured token usage. hy3-free was selected because it is the model used by the prior opencode-capacity-curve experiment, keeping the provider surface comparable, and because pre-freeze capability probes showed a non-degenerate acceptance spread on this benchmark (2 of 3 probed tasks accepted, 1 rejected), so accepted throughput is measurable rather than uniformly zero.
modelSelection.probeDisclosure: These probes ran before the freeze, outside the experiment, solely to select a model and confirm the benchmark is executable end-to-end by a real agent. The benchmark was not modified after observing them, and their runs are not counted in any reported result.

priorEvidence.note: Recorded for descriptive comparison only. Prior scaling results come from the synthetic ledger-kit workload and must not be pooled numerically with this experiment.

prohibitedConclusions: The current host represents production agent infrastructure.
The observed result generalizes to all coding agents.
The observed result generalizes to all repositories.
intendedCommand: node apps/cli/dist/index.js benchmark-materialize --manifest benchmarks/real-work-v1/manifest.json --repository semver-core --destination <clean-semver-core-checkout> --tasks-output <tasks.json> && node apps/cli/dist/index.js run --repo <clean-semver-core-checkout> --tasks <tasks.json> --workers 1,2 --repetitions 3 --seed 20260822 --agent opencode --agent-model opencode/hy3-free --order repetition-major --output experiments/real-work-external-validity-v1
